title: Pattanam excavation find record (candidate site of ancient Muziris)
language_note: English-language excavation reporting by the Kerala Council for Historical Research (KCHR); no single regional-language primary text — included as an archaeological/artefact anchor (Pillar 4).
date: Mediterranean-linked layers: 100 BCE - 400 CE; site occupation from c. 1000 BCE
findspot: Pattanam, near North Paravur, Ernakulam district, Kerala, India; excavated 2007-2014 by KCHR

contested_citations: FOR — Kerala Council for Historical Research, Pattanam 7th season excavation handbook (2013): Roman amphora and terra sigillata sherds, and a 1983 Roman coin hoard ~9.7 km inland, adduced in support of the port identification. Archived at https://web.archive.org/web/20160304031410/http://www.keralahistory.ac.in/pdf2013/pattanam_7th_season_handbook1.pdf

AGAINST — PROVISIONAL, AND MUST BE REPLACED WITH A PUBLISHED SOURCE. This record's own `notes` field states that the Archaeological Survey of India has urged caution over the Pattanam DNA results pending further sampling. That is a summary in our own corpus, not a citation to published scholarship, and it does not yet meet the two-sides requirement in the spirit the rule intends. Recorded here so the contested flag is not carried on a single side; replace with the ASI statement or a published sceptical treatment.
findspot_places.note: Confirmed against the Pleiades places snapshot of 2026-08-10: Pleiades 50146 'Muziris' sits at 10.154, 76.213 — which IS Pattanam — feature types 'settlement, port', attested -30..640, locationPrecision 'precise'. Pleiades has therefore ALREADY ADOPTED the identification this record treats as open, and marks it precise. The coordinate is used because it is the excavation site; the label 'Muziris' is what is contested. Pleiades holds no entry titled 'Pattanam'.

original_text_excerpt: Mediterranean objects (100 BC to 400 AD): Amphora and terra sigillata shards; fragments of Roman glass pillar bowls; and gaming counters. West Asian, South Arabian, and Mesopotamian objects (300 BC to 1000 AD): turquoise glazed pottery; torpedo jar fragments; frankincense crumbs. Most remarkable: a fired brick wharf complex with nine teak bollards and a mummified 6-metre dugout canoe (Artocarpus hirsutus).
original_text_note: Adapted from Wikipedia's 'Muziris' article (Archeological excavations), which synthesizes the Kerala Council for Historical Research's season reports. An earlier version of this note promised to pull the KCHR handbook's own text during ingestion; that was never done, and on 2026-09-23 the promise was withdrawn rather than left standing.
citation_original: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muziris -- the 'Archeological excavations' section, whose prose this record's text adapts. The KCHR handbook this field used to name (https://web.archive.org/web/20160304031410/http://www.keralahistory.ac.in/pdf2013/pattanam_7th_season_handbook1.pdf) is among that article's sources, not this record's.
notes: Physical corroboration for the textual Muziris cluster (southasia-01 through -03): Roman amphora/terra sigillata shards and a 1983 hoard of Roman coins found ~9.7 km inland support the port identification. DNA analysis of skeletal remains also shows West Eurasian genetic imprints, though ASI has urged caution pending further sampling — worth flagging as a contested/uncertain claim in the eval harness rather than an established fact.
